title: Source-minted review dispatches under the chg root

story.as_a: fleet machine's chgd dispatching a review
story.i_want_to: obtain a review key under the source's chg root for one (change_id, revision)
story.so_that: the reviewer's verdict satisfies US-47.5's chg review custody with no process holding a standing root key

rationale: A dispatch key lives at most 14400 s and the operator key cannot mint under a root outside its lineage, so Epic 47 §6's chg-server-holds-the-root design has no holder. loopctl#1014 comment 3, question 2.

acceptance_criteria.description: POST /api/v1/change_events/:source_id/review_dispatch with {change_id, revision}, authenticated as the change-events webhook, mints a child dispatch of the source's chg_root_dispatch_id (role :orchestrator, so review_complete's exact_role gate admits it) and answers 201 {dispatch_id, api_key, expires_at}.

The change must have an applied submitted event for that revision under the source; otherwise 422 revision_not_submitted. A source with no chg_root_dispatch_id, or whose root is revoked, gets the change-events 401.

One live review dispatch per (source, change_id, revision): a second request revokes the earlier dispatch and mints a fresh one ONLY while the earlier one has recorded no review; after a verdict it answers 409 review_already_recorded. A lost response is therefore retryable and a recorded verdict is never re-mintable.

The minted key passes US-47.5 unchanged: it is a strict descendant of the root (chg_reviewer_required passes), is refused claim and report (chg_root_review_only) and verify/reject (chg_root_cannot_verify). No custody gate is loosened.
The mint is appended to the tenant audit chain with source_id, change_id, revision and dispatch_id. The root dispatch's own key expiry does not matter; only its revocation does.

docs/chain-of-custody-v2.md and CLAUDE.md's chg-dispatched reviews paragraph state the trust this moves: whoever holds change_events_secret can mint reviewers for that source, as chg-server could before; loopctl proves the source minted the key, not that the job ran apart from the implementer.

test_cases.name: mint and record
preconditions: a story bound to a change with submitted revision 1, reported done
steps: review_complete with the returned key and commit_sha of revision 1

test_cases.name: re-mint before and after a verdict
steps: record a review with the second key

test_cases.name: the key cannot verify or claim

technical_notes: Mint through Dispatches with the root as parent on a server-side path that does not consult caller lineage, because the caller is the source's HMAC, not a key. That path is reachable only from this controller; never expose it to a key-authenticated route.
Hold the source and root FOR SHARE in the mint's transaction, as Intake.hold_chg_source/3 does for events.
